analysis.summary: Shanti Gold International Limited held its Q4 and FY26 earnings conference call on May 22, 2026, discussing robust operational and financial performance, including record quarterly and annual revenues. Management highlighted strategic capacity expansions in Mumbai (Marol) and Jaipur to support growing demand from organized retail jewellers and new product lines like Turkish jewellery and Mangalsutras. The company transitioned its inventory valuation method from FIFO to weighted average cost (WAC) starting April 1, 2024. For the upcoming year, management guided for 30% to 40% volume growth and 60% to 70% value-based growth. Shanti Gold International Limited released its investor presentation for Q4 and FY26, highlighting significant financial growth with Q4 FY26 revenue reaching Rs 658.9 Cr and annual FY26 revenue at Rs 2,018.7 Cr.

guidance.claim: Management expects around 30% to 40% growth in terms of volume and around 60% to 70% growth in terms of value for the coming year.
guidance.quote: So this year, i.e current coming year, it will be around 30% to 40% growth in terms of volume and around 60%-70% growth in terms of value

guidance.claim: Management stated that the sustainable net profit (PAT) business margin is around 4% plus.
guidance.quote: This margin would be around 4% and all, which we've been maintaining that 4% plus and all.

demand_outlook.claim: Despite elevated gold prices, overall demand trends remained resilient across key markets and customer segments, particularly in wedding and occasions-led jewellery.
demand_outlook.quote: Despite elevated gold prices during the year, overall demand trends remained resilient across key markets and customer segments. We continue to witness healthy transactions, particularly in wedding and occasions-led jewellery categories.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted an increasing outsourcing preference among organized jewellers and retailers as they expand footprints and optimize inventory.
demand_outlook.quote: One of the most encouraging trends we are witnessing today is the increasing outsourcing preference among organized jewellers, retailers, as retailers continue to focus on expanding their footprint, inventory optimizing, and faster design cycles.

demand_outlook.claim: India remains one of the world's largest consumers of gold jewellery supported by cultural affinity, rising disposable incomes, and wedding demands.
demand_outlook.quote: India remains one of the world's largest consumers of gold jewellery, strongly supported by strong cultural affinity, rising disposable incomes, wedding demands, and increasing preference for branded jewellery at the same time.

demand_outlook.claim: Growing disposable income drives gold as a status symbol and investment.
demand_outlook.quote: Growing disposable income drives gold as status symbol & investment

demand_outlook.claim: Seasonal demand arises from weddings, Diwali, and harvest festivals.
demand_outlook.quote: Seasonal demand from weddings, Diwali & harvest festivals

demand_outlook.claim: Unique Indian designs are attracting global buyers, presenting export growth potential.
demand_outlook.quote: Unique Indian designs attracting global buyers; export growth potential

demand_outlook.claim: Branded players are driving consumer trust in the jewellery market.
demand_outlook.quote: Branded players (Tanishq, Kalyan, Malabar) driving consumer trust

demand_outlook.claim: Monthly jewellery investment schemes improve affordability.
demand_outlook.quote: Monthly jewellery investment schemes improve affordability

capex_expansion.claim: The new Marol facility in Mumbai will add approximately 4,000 kilo per annum of manufacturing capacity.
capex_expansion.quote: Our existing Andheri manufacturing facility with an installed capacity of approximately 2,700 kilo per annum has been operating at healthy utilization levels in line with the growth of our new Marol facility in Mumbai, which will add approximately 4,000 kilo per annum of manufacturing capacity.

capex_expansion.claim: The 1,200 kilo per annum capacity addition announced during the IPO at Jaipur continues to progress in line with expectations.
capex_expansion.quote: In addition, the 1,200 kilo per annum capacity addition announced during an IPO at Jaipur, continues to progress in line with expectations.

capex_expansion.claim: The Marol factory is expected to start in a month or so, while the Jaipur factory is expected to start around September or October.
capex_expansion.quote: So see, our new factory is almost ready, which is going to be like in a month or so for Marol factory, and I guess Jaipur factory should be starting by around September, October now.

capex_expansion.claim: The upcoming Jaipur facility adds 1,200 kg pa capacity, bringing total capacity to 3,900 kg pa.
A new Mumbai facility is planned to add 4,000 kg capacity.
capex_expansion.quote: New Mumbai facility adding 4,000 kg capacity

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA for Q4 FY26 stood at INR 67.01 crores with an EBITDA margin of 10.17%, improving by 306 basis points year-on-year.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA for Q4 FY26 stood at INR 67.01 crores as compared to INR 21.12 crores in Q4 FY25, registering a growth of 217.26% Y-oY. EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 10.17% as compared to 7.10% in the corresponding period last year, improving by 306 basis points.

margins_costs.claim: The company transitioned its inventory valuation methodology from FIFO to the weighted average cost (WAC) method with retrospective effect from April 01, 2024.
margins_costs.quote: The company has transitioned its inventory valuation methodology from the First In, First Out, FIFO method to the weighted average cost WAC method with retrospective effect from April 01, 2024.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA margins for FY26 stood at 9.86% as compared to 8.13% in FY25, improving by 173 basis points.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA margins for FY26 stood at 9.86% as compared to 8.13% in FY25, improving by 173 basis points.

orders_capacity.claim: The company's existing Andheri manufacturing facility has an installed capacity of approximately 2,700 kilo per annum.
orders_capacity.quote: Our existing Andheri manufacturing facility with an installed capacity of approximately 2,700 kilo per annum has been operating at healthy utilization levels in line with the growth of our new Marol facility in Mumbai, which will add approximately 4,000 kilo per annum of manufacturing capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The current capacity utilization of the existing factory is around 65%.
Once operational, capacity additions will take total installed manufacturing capacity to nearly 7,900 kilogram per annum.
orders_capacity.quote: Once operational, this addition will take our total installed manufacturing capacity to nearly 7,900 kilogram per annum, positioning us strongly for the next phase of scalable growth.

capital_allocation.claim: The company maintains a debt-equity ratio of 0.36.
capital_allocation.quote: Yes, and as far as the value again, if you see the metrics also, my debt-equity is at 0.36.

capital_allocation.claim: Management stated that the company is comfortable going up to a debt-to-equity ratio of 1:1 to fuel future growth expansion.
capital_allocation.quote: To answer your question, maximum at this point if I say, we should be comfortable at going at 1:1. That's what we are aiming for now to fuel the future growth expansion.

risks_headwinds.claim: The incorporation timeline for the Dubai subsidiary has been extended to June 2026 due to geopolitical conflicts.
risks_headwinds.quote: So due to all these wars and all, it is extended for a couple of months more ahead now because the situation, geopolitical things are not good.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that geopolitical situations and ongoing wars create volatility and uncertainty across the world.
risks_headwinds.quote: So, due to again Iran war with Israel and US and all, so things are not good, means lot of volatility is there and things are not good across the world.

risks_headwinds.claim: Forward-looking statements are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and assumptions that are difficult to predict.
risks_headwinds.quote: Such forward-looking statements are not guarantees of future performance and are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and assumptions that are difficult to predict.

management_commitments.quote: • Targeting underpenetrated markets with rising demand

management_commitments.quote: • Building a balanced pan-India revenue mix

management_commitments.quote: • Focus on high-potential USA & UAE corridors
